section_summary: This section contains English-language monitoring transcripts of Radio Tokyo broadcasts from May and June 1941, together with two FBI cover letters forwarding broadcast translations to the State Department. The broadcasts report the war in Europe and Asia and include commentary on American policy, the German invasion of the Soviet Union, and Japan’s relations with China. Several talks address Japanese people living overseas.

subfiles.title: Radio Tokyo English-language news and music broadcast, concluding pages
subfiles.about: The concluding portion of a broadcast gives international and China-war news, then a programme of Japanese songs.
subfiles.summary: The news covers Cyprus, Syria, Ireland, China, Crete, U.S. policy, and Japanese cultural and military affairs. A Japanese folk-song programme follows.

subfiles.title: Radio Tokyo English-language broadcast of May 29, 1941
subfiles.about: A Radio Tokyo programme presents news and a recorded lecture on the development of Japan's national army.
subfiles.summary: The news reports a Japan–Iran treaty, Japanese reactions to Roosevelt's fireside chat, stalled talks with the Dutch East Indies, fighting in China and Crete, and other war developments. The broadcast closes with a recorded lecture on Japan's transition from a feudal state to a national state.

subfiles.title: FBI cover letter forwarding translated JZK broadcasts
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FBI forwards translations of Japanese-language broadcasts attributed to Station JZK.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme of June 20, 1941
subfiles.about: News, commentary on U.S.–German relations, and a talk to Japanese listeners in Hawaii are transcribed.
subfiles.summary: The programme reports Wang Jingwei's visit, Japanese military operations, European fighting, and U.S. financial measures against Axis powers. Its commentary predicts worsening U.S.–German relations. Shigeharu Kimura's talk assures overseas Japanese that Japan can withstand shortages and urges national unity.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme of June 23, 1941
subfiles.about: The programme reports the German invasion of the Soviet Union and includes an address to overseas Japanese.
subfiles.summary: Reports describe the first days of the German–Soviet war and reactions across Europe and Asia. Japanese domestic and China-war news follows. A long address by a National Support Society official praises Japanese migration and presents imperial expansion as Asian emancipation.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme of June 24, 1941
subfiles.about: The broadcast concentrates on the German–Soviet war and its expected effects on Britain, the United States, China, and Japan.
subfiles.summary: The programme reports Japanese cabinet discussions, Wang Jingwei's visit, air raids in China, and competing German and Soviet claims about the invasion. It surveys diplomatic responses and offers extended commentary on the war's causes and possible global effects.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme of June 25, 1941
subfiles.about: The programme covers Japanese policy meetings, Wang Jingwei's departure, and further developments in the German–Soviet war.
subfiles.summary: Reports include Japanese leadership meetings, Wang Jingwei's return to Nanking, military news from China, and conflicting claims from the Eastern Front. Commentary promotes the Konoe–Wang joint declaration and broadcasts Konoe's welcome to Wang.

subfiles.title: FBI cover letter forwarding Tokyo broadcast translations
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: The FBI forwards translated Tokyo broadcasts dated June 2 and July 2–15, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Cover letter transmitting translated radio transcripts.

subfiles.title: Station JZK programme of June 2, 1941
subfiles.about: A talk explains the Overseas Japanese Central Society, followed by news from China, the Mediterranean, Iraq, Mexico, and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lieutenant General Yoshiyuki Suzuki describes the society's services for Japanese residents abroad. News items cover Japanese operations in China, the battle for Crete, the Iraq conflict, French protests over attacks near North Africa, Mexican relations with the United States, and Japanese domestic affairs.
